description:
We are a team passionate about technology, astronomy, space exploration, and science. We enjoy programming, AI, and building creative solutions that make learning more interactive and engaging.

We are looking for motivated teammates with skills in software development, UI/UX design, 3D modeling, animation, scientific research, or storytelling. We believe in teamwork, creativity, and turning innovative ideas into reality.
summary:
We developed an interactive, browser-based educational web application for the NASA Space Apps Challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, where iconic spacecraft left on the Moon and Mars narrate their own histories across five chapters: who I am, why I was sent, how I worked, what we learned, and what happened to me.

Featuring six core lunar and Martian explorers alongside missions illustrating diverse planetary fates, the platform dynamically adapts to two age groups—offering interactive scenes and games for younger students, and deeper analysis of scientific instruments, engineering challenges, and observation versus interpretation for older learners.

This project is important because it transforms dense technical mission archives into relatable, engaging stories while maintaining strict scientific rigor. Every record links directly to verified NASA sources, explicitly separates last contact from official mission termination, and leaves unconfirmed data blank. Powered entirely by lightweight, editable JSON files without requiring servers, accounts, or paid APIs, it provides a free, easily maintainable educational resource for classrooms worldwide.
details:
How it works: MAJARRA is an interactive, browser-based educational web app for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Iconic spacecraft left on the Moon and Mars (plus other planetary fates) narrate their own histories in five chapters: who I am, why I was sent, how I worked, what we learned, and what happened to me.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

  • Tailored Learning: Adapts dynamically to two age groups—offering interactive scenes and games for younger students, and deeper analysis of scientific instruments, engineering challenges, and observation vs. interpretation for older students.
  • Accessibility: Runs entirely in the browser via lightweight JSON files with no servers, accounts, or paid APIs, making verified space science accessible and easily maintainable for classrooms worldwide.

Tools & Technologies: Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and structured JSON files, alongside digital UI/UX design and collaboration tools.

Creativity & Key Factors:

  • Creativity: Personifies abandoned hardware as first-person narrators, transforming dry mission logs into engaging, emotional journeys.
  • Scientific Rigor: Links every fact to verified NASA sources, separates last contact from official mission end, and leaves unconfirmed data blank.
